questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to replace the word in brackets. The author's writing was so captivating that readers were [enthralled], while the other book left them completely uninterested.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to replace the word in brackets.
The author's writing was so captivating that readers were [enthralled], while the other book left them completely uninterested.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "enthralled" means to capture the fascinated attention of someone; to hold spellbound. (मंत्रमुग्ध करना)
    • Example: The magician's performance enthralled the audience.
  • "Bored" refers to feeling weary and impatient because one is unoccupied or lacks interest in one's current activity. (उबाऊ)
    • Example: She was bored by the lecture on ancient history.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'enthralled' is 'bored'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Interested (रुचि): Showing curiosity or concern about something or someone.
    • Example: He was very interested in learning about different cultures.
  • Agreement (समझौता): Harmony or accordance in opinion or feeling.
    • Example: They reached an agreement after hours of negotiation.
  • Intrigued (जिज्ञासु): Arouse the curiosity or interest of; fascinate.
    • Example: The detective was intrigued by the mysterious case.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. This library building is very high and has 25 floors.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
This library building is very high and has 25 floors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Low.

Key Points

  • The word "high" means something that is of great vertical extent or elevated. (ऊँचा)
    • Example: The high mountain peaks were covered with snow.
  • "Low" refers to something that is situated not far above the ground or that is not very tall. (निचा)
    • Example: The low fence around the garden barely reached my knees.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'high' is 'low'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Low.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Sturdy (मजबूत): Strongly and solidly built.
    • Example: The sturdy table can hold a lot of weight.
  • Hale (स्वस्थ): In good health, especially in old age.
    • Example: Despite his age, he remains hale and active.
  • Elevated (उन्नत): Situated or placed higher than the surrounding area.
    • Example: The elevated platform gave us a better view of the performance.

questions.question: In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement. O: that the Soviet army had liberated P: from the fascist forces came under Q: the east European countries R: the control of the USSR S: after the Second World War
questions.questionHtml:
In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent
statement.
O: that the Soviet army had liberated
P: from the fascist forces came under
Q: the east European countries
R: the control of the USSR
S: after the Second World War
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The statement discusses the historical context of the Soviet army's actions after the Second World War.
  • Part S is the first part as it sets the time frame, "after the Second World War":
    • "after the Second World War"
  • Part Q follows next to introduce the subject, "the east European countries":
    • "the east European countries"
  • Part O is the third part as it describes the action taken by the Soviet army, "that the Soviet army had liberated":
    • "that the Soviet army had liberated"
  • Part P comes next detailing what happened to these countries, "from the fascist forces came under":
    • "from the fascist forces came under"
  • Part R concludes by explaining the outcome, "the control of the USSR":
    • "the control of the USSR"
  • The correct sequence is SQOPR.
 
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"After the Second World War, the east European countries that the Soviet army had liberated from the fascist forces came under the control of the USSR."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Ranveer never has the habit of making a beeline for his academic activities.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Ranveer never has the habit of making a beeline for his academic activities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "beeline" means to go straight towards something quickly and directly. (सीधे और जल्दी जाना)
    • Example: As soon as the gates opened, the fans made a beeline for the stage.
  • "going straight and quick" accurately describes the action of making a beeline. (सीधे और जल्दी जाना)
    • Example: When the lunch bell rang, the students made a beeline for the cafeteria.
  • Hence, the correct substitution for "making a beeline" is "going straight and quick".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Behaving abnormally (असामान्य रूप से व्यवहार करना): Acting in a way that is not typical or usual.
    • Example: He was behaving abnormally after hearing the shocking news.
  • Selecting inconsiderately (अविवेकपूर्ण चयन करना): Choosing something without careful thought or consideration.
    • Example: She was selecting inconsiderately when she picked her team without knowing their skills.
  • Immediately responding to things (तुरंत प्रतिक्रिया देना): Reacting to something at once.
    • Example: He has a habit of immediately responding to things without thinking them through.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Rohit did not slap Kunal.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Rohit did not slap Kunal.

options.text: Kunal was not being slapped by Rohit.
options.html: Kunal was not being slapped by Rohit.

options.text: Kunal had not been slapped by Rohit.
options.html: Kunal had not been slapped by Rohit.

options.text: Kunal was not slapped by Rohit.
options.html: Kunal was not slapped by Rohit.

options.text: Kunal has not been slapped by Rohit.
options.html: Kunal has not been slapped by Rohit.

questions.solution:
```html
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "Rohit did not slap Kunal."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "Kunal" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "did not slap" to "was not slapped" (simple past passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Rohit."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "Kunal was not slapped by Rohit."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "Kunal was not being slapped by Rohit." – Incorrect tense (past continuous passive).
  • Option 2: "Kunal had not been slapped by Rohit." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
  • Option 4: "Kunal has not been slapped by Rohit." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
```

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The company understood that these small protests of employees regarding low wages were just the tip of the iceberg .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
The company understood that these small protests of employees regarding low wages were just the tip of the iceberg.

options.text: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is non-existent
options.html: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is non-existent

options.text: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is solvable
options.html: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is solvable

options.text: A large part of a problem which is really noticeable
options.html: A large part of a problem which is really noticeable

options.text: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater
options.html: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The idiom "the tip of the iceberg" means:
    • A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater. (समस्या का एक छोटा, ध्यान देने योग्य भाग, जिसका कुल आकार वास्तव में बहुत बड़ा है।)
  • Example: The corruption scandal involving the mayor was just the tip of the iceberg; there were many more officials involved in illegal activities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is non-existent. (समस्या का एक छोटा, ध्यान देने योग्य भाग, जिसका कुल आकार अस्तित्वहीन है।)
    • Example: He thought the minor complaint was the entire issue, not realizing it was a small, noticeable part of a problem that didn't exist.
  • Option 2: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is solvable. (समस्या का एक छोटा, ध्यान देने योग्य भाग, जिसका कुल आकार हल करने योग्य है।)
    • Example: The broken window was just a small, noticeable part of a problem that was easily solvable.
  • Option 3: A large part of a problem which is really noticeable. (एक समस्या का बड़ा हिस्सा जो वास्तव में ध्यान देने योग्य है।)
    • Example: The visible pollution is a large part of the problem which is really noticeable to everyone.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. The world’s biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico. B. It is called Arecibo dish. C. It was built 40 years ago. D. It is also 300 metres across.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.
A. The world’s biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico.
B. It is called Arecibo dish.
C. It was built 40 years ago.
D. It is also 300 metres across.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The sequence starts with a general introduction.
  • Part A is the first because it introduces the radio telescope, "The world’s biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico.":
    • "The world’s biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico."
  • Part B follows next to provide its name, "It is called Arecibo dish.":
    • "It is called Arecibo dish."
  • Part D is the third to give historical context, "It is also 300 metres across." :
    • "It is also 300 metres across"
  • Part C comes last to add specific detail, "It was built 40 years ago.":
    • "​It was built 40 years ago."
  • The correct sequence is ABDC.
 
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"The world’s biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico. It is called Arecibo dish. It is also 300 metres across. It was built 40 years ago."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The chair I have bought recently is costly than what I bought last year.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The chair I have bought recently is costly than what I bought last year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
Key Points
  • The underlined segment "is costly" needs to be replaced with a comparative form to correctly convey the comparison being made.
  • The correct comparative form of "costly" is "costlier."
  • The sentence should read, "The chair I have bought recently is costlier than what I bought last year."
Therefore, the correct answer is 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "The chair I have bought recently is costlier than what I bought last year."
 
Additional Information
  • 1: "is the costliest" – This implies a superlative comparison, which is not suitable here as the comparison is between two items.
  • 3: "was costly" – This changes the tense and does not provide the necessary comparative structure.
  • 4: "will be costly" – This changes both the tense and the comparative meaning, making it incorrect.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. Akshaya ___________ hard for the entrance exam and received a high score.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank.

Akshaya ___________ hard for the entrance exam and received a high score.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'D' i.e. studied.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the verb should be in the past tense to match the action that has already been completed.
  • Option 1, "studies," is in the present tense and does not fit the context of a completed action.
  • Option 2, "has studied," is in the present perfect tense and implies that the action has relevance to the present, which is not suitable here.
  • Option 3, "was studied," is in the passive voice and does not fit the context.
  • Option 4, "studied," is in the simple past tense and correctly completes the sentence, indicating an action that has been completed.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: Akshaya studied hard for the entrance exam and received a high score.

Additional Information

  • The simple past tense is used to express actions that have been completed in the past.
  • Ensure that the verb tense in the sentence matches the time frame of the action described.
  • Example: She completed the project on time and received praise from her supervisor.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. His parents didn’t allow him to enrol in the arts college because he is a dabbler in arts, science or literature.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
His parents didn’t allow him to enrol in the arts college because he is a dabbler in arts, science or literature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "dabbler" refers to someone who takes part in an activity in a casual or superficial way, without serious commitment or knowledge. (शौकिया)
    • Example: He is just a dabbler in photography and doesn't take it seriously.
  • "Dilettante" refers to a person who cultivates an area of interest, such as the arts, without real commitment or knowledge. (शौकिया)
    • Example: As a dilettante, she dabbles in various artistic hobbies but never focuses on one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Connoisseur (विशेषज्ञ): An expert judge in matters of taste.
    • Example: He is a connoisseur of fine wines.
  • Taciturn (मितभाषी): Reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little.
    • Example: She was a taciturn woman who kept her thoughts to herself.
  • Ignoramus (मूर्ख): An ignorant or stupid person.
    • Example: Don't listen to him; he's an ignoramus when it comes to technology.

questions.questionHtml:

I do not have any access to the information in this matter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Denial.  

The meaning of the word "access" is the ability to approach, enter, or use something.  
The meaning of the word "denial" is the refusal or rejection of access, permission, or acceptance.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The teacher asked him not to keep disturbing the class, but it had no affect.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
The teacher asked him not to keep disturbing the class, but it had no affect.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
Key Points
  • The word "affect" is a verb that means to influence something.
  • The correct word to use here is "effect," which is a noun that means a result or outcome.
  • Thus, the phrase should read "but it had no effect."
  • Therefore, the error is in part 1 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "The teacher asked him not to keep disturbing the class, but it had no effect."
 
Additional Information
  • 2: "him not to keep" – This part is grammatically correct and does not contain any errors.
  • 3: "disturbing the class," – This part is grammatically correct and does not contain any errors.
  • 4: "The teacher asked" – This part is grammatically correct and does not contain any errors.
  • 1: "but it had no affect." – The error here is the incorrect use of “affect” instead of “effect.”
